what: Real pointer drag (mouse down + ~250 moves, no artificial pacing) at deviceScaleFactor 2 on the what-if slider; measures main-thread health. Reproduce: cd web && node stress-drag.mjs <path-to-xlsx> --dpr=2
workbook: corpus/work/fuse-bins/cc-binaries/56cbca12-9c02-49e5-a064-53129669df80 (58,389 formulas; selected assumption cone: 390 cells, schedule build ~850-910 ms)
machine: 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1250U, WSL2, headless Chromium (playwright)

after_worker_engine.note: synthetic events at 16ms pacing -- too gentle to expose the real defect

note: The engine (two wasm Sessions) runs in Web Workers; the what-if slider is a latest-wins pipeline with at most one evaluation in flight. Zero long tasks means the main thread was never blocked >50ms at any point during the drag.
root_cause_found_2026_08_09: ensureCanvas read the canvas's logical height back from its own height attribute, but assigning canvas.height REWRITES that attribute -- so at devicePixelRatio>1 the backing store multiplied by dpr on every paint (180 -> 360 -> 720 ...) until the tab blanked. Stable at dpr 1, which is why headless tests passed. Logical height now lives in data-h; dpr is capped at 2.

after_render_fix_dpr2.note: identical to a slider with every listener removed -- the interaction now costs nothing measurable
